answer: Work history locks for 90 days before it counts toward standing, and a peer disagreement dilutes the payout instead of voiding it. Because dilution is shared across the panel, one honest dissent costs the claimant a fraction rather than everything, which keeps jurors willing to show up. A thousand-name farm must hold a thousand histories open for three months before the first payment, and every claim is rechecked by someone with nothing to gain. The falcon here is time: 90 days of rent against a karst that may stay hollow.
